title: Declarative region assignments, retention inheritance, and evidence zipper for hosted endpoints
creator: Ava Patel
description: Add a declarative region-assignment API and a retention-profile inheritance model for hosted endpoints, plus an "evidence zipper" that composes attestable exports (logs, route decisions, retention artifacts) for audits. The goal is to let customers express a single policy (location + retention) per tenant or endpoint and automatically generate an auditable package when requested.
background: Customers ask for simpler controls to ensure data stays in allowed geographies while retaining the ability to specify retention defaults and exceptions per endpoint. Existing features are ad-hoc: policy pins live in multiple places and evidence exports are manual and partial. This ticket consolidates a declarative policy surface, runtime enforcement primitives, and an automated export builder.
objectives: Design a minimal declarative schema (TenantPolicy / EndpointPolicy) with precedence rules
Implement an API for setting region assignments and retention profiles (TTL + retention tiers)
Runtime: enforce routing decisions based on policy and emit structured decision traces
Build evidence zipper: produce compact, signed bundles that include decision logs, retention manifests, and delivery receipts
Support a soft-affinity mode for gradual rollouts and a strict-lock mode for compliance-required tenants
scope: Hosted API control plane + runtime hooks + evidence export service. UI surface: policy create/edit flow and evidence download button in tenant settings. Minimal SDK updates for setting endpoint policy programmatically.
out_of_scope: Dedicated and Private control planes (follow-up), long-term archival pipeline changes, automated legal attestation beyond generated artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Create/Update/Delete TenantPolicy via REST and Console UI
Routing honors policy: requests from a tenant with strict-lock=eu are never routed outside eu-* regions
Retention inheritance: endpoint without explicit retention uses tenant default; exceptions supported per route
Evidence zipper produces a signed ZIP containing decision-log.json, retention-manifest.json, and an index with hashes
Audit: evidence ZIP generation completes within SLA (<= 2 minutes for <10k request traces) and is downloadable from console
success_metrics: Time-to-configure: reduce average steps to enable residency for a new tenant from 12 -> 4
Export completeness: >95% of audited requests include a matching decision trace in evidence bundles
Customer reported compliance incidents related to residency drop to zero for tenants using strict-lock mode
engineering_notes: Runtime will add a PolicyEvaluator component that attaches a trace header (X-Redwood-Residency) to requests and writes decision events to the residency-trace topic. Evidence zipper will pull traces, query retention metadata service, assemble artifacts, compute SHA256 index, and sign with the platform key. Consider rate-limiting exports and indexing for large tenants.
rollout_plan: 1) Beta: opt-in flag (soft-affinity) for 10 pilot tenants. 2) Collect traces and iterate on export format. 3) Add strict-lock enforcement and UI guardrails. 4) Gradual rollout to all hosted tenants with migration tool to convert existing pin settings.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Overly strict routing could increase latency if regional capacity is constrained. Mitigation: implement capacity-aware soft-fallback and circuit-breaker with audit record when fallback used.
Risk: Evidence zip may expose PII if traces contain user data. Mitigation: filter Personally Identifiable fields by default and include redaction metadata in the manifest.
Risk: Signing keys compromise. Mitigation: KMS rotation policy and short-lived export tokens; require security review before GA.
